fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Paul never says he picked this job himself. He says he is "…called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God…" (1 Corinthians 1:1). An apostle is someone sent out by Christ. So the calling came by God's will, and I'd say that takes a lot of pressure off the résumé.

Yes, friend! Paul says they are "…sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy…" (1 Corinthians 1:2). Sanctified means set apart for God. He says it to the church in Corinth, in the very first lines of the letter. That's a big word for a greeting, and he puts it right up front.

Free sounds good, friend, but that's not Paul's word here. He says they are "…sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy…" (1 Corinthians 1:2). Holy means set apart for God. Free is a word I'd happily put on a cookie box, but this verse has a different one.

Right, friend. Paul says, "I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus." (1 Corinthians 1:4). His thanks goes to God, and the reason is the grace God has given them. It's the same word, grace, that he just used in his greeting. Paul starts the letter with thank-you before anything else.
Earthly isn't what Paul writes, friend. He says, "…you do not lack any spiritual gift…" (1 Corinthians 1:7). The word is spiritual. Not one of them is missing.
Royal sounds fancy, friend, but that's not Paul's word. He says, "…you do not lack any spiritual gift…" (1 Corinthians 1:7). The word is spiritual. Not one of them is missing.

Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36), friend, but he's not in this verse. Paul says they eagerly await "…the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:7). The one they're waiting for is Jesus Himself. Good name, but not the one in this line.

Gabriel is an angel who brought a message to Mary (Luke 1:26-28), friend, but he's not who Paul means. Paul says they eagerly await "…the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:7). The one being revealed is Jesus. An angel at the door is great, but it's the Lord they're waiting for.

Hold on, friend, this one is true. Paul writes, "He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:8). Look at who does the sustaining. It says "He will," so the holding up is His doing, not theirs.

Jealous isn't the word Paul uses here, friend. He says, "God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful." (1 Corinthians 1:9). Faithful is the word he picks. It's a warm way to wrap up the greeting.

Not hidden, friend. Paul says, "God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful." (1 Corinthians 1:9). He's the One who called them, and Paul says He is faithful. I spent years stuck in the back of a drawer, but that was me, not Him.
